frontMatter.welcome:
We’re thrilled to have you as part of the family! As a new member, you join us on our journey of heritage, innovation, and sustainability. We believe each employee contributes directly to our growth, and we’re excited for the fresh perspectives you’ll bring. Starting here is the first step toward a rewarding career, where your work will make a positive impact in the jute industry and beyond.
Our company values – Commitment, Integrity, and Excellence – shape every action we take. They drive us to deliver high-quality, eco-friendly products, to support our clients’ diverse needs, and to maintain sustainable practices that help our communities and the environment thrive. We encourage you to embody these values as they’ll guide your journey with us and foster personal and professional success.
Your first few weeks may be a whirlwind of training and new information, so take it step by step. This handbook was created to outline expectations, company policies, and the programs available to support you. We’re here to make sure your experience is enriching, enjoyable, and meaningful. Welcome aboard!

frontMatter.about:
Ananya Jute Mills, based in West Bengal, has a deep-rooted legacy in the jute industry, with origins tracing back to 1879. The company evolved through significant structural changes and now stands as a leader in sustainable jute manufacturing. Today, our product offerings range from traditional jute sacks to specialized, treated fabrics, geo-textiles, and consumer products, catering to industrial and consumer markets alike. Our two major manufacturing units in Howrah uphold our commitment to excellence, while our dedication to innovation allows us to meet the changing demands of a modern, environmentally conscious market.
Our leadership team brings over six decades of expertise to the business, continually expanding our focus on eco-friendly practices. We prioritize aligning our products with global green standards, ensuring that Ananya Jute Mills remains at the forefront of sustainable manufacturing. This legacy not only reflects our commitment to quality but also guides our path toward a future that is both profitable and sustainable for our stakeholders and communities.
frontMatter.purpose:
This handbook serves as a thorough guide to your employment at Gloster Limited. It contains essential details about our policies, procedures, benefits, and available resources. We strongly recommend reviewing it in full and keeping it handy for future reference. If you have any questions or need further clarification on any section, please feel free to contact your manager or the Human Resources team. Familiarity with this handbook is key to ensuring a smooth and successful experience with Gloster Limited.
We are committed to protecting workers' rights and improving labor conditions for everyone involved with the company. We make sure to follow all local laws and industry standards.
- No Child Labor: We do not employ anyone under 18 years old. We ensure that no one is working under the legal working age.
- No Forced Labor: All workers are employed voluntarily. No one is forced to work against their will. All employees can leave their jobs at any time with reasonable notice, and we don’t make anyone stay if they don’t want to.
- Safe Workplace: We prioritize the safety and health of everyone at work. We take all necessary actions to prevent accidents and injuries. Our workplace is regularly inspected to ensure it is free from hazards.
- Freedom to Join Unions: Employees have the right to join or form a union without fear of discrimination or retaliation. We support employees in making this choice.
- Equal Treatment: We treat all employees fairly and ensure that no one faces discrimination. We also support disadvantaged groups when they meet the qualifications. We make sure that people are hired, paid, and promoted based on skills, qualifications, and performance, without bias.

chapters.title: Probation and Confirmation
chapters.text:
## Understanding the probation period:
- New employees are placed on a 3-month probation period during which their performance is monitored and evaluated regularly. Feedback is provided to ensure the employee’s success and improvement if needed.
- Post-Probation Confirmation: If the employee successfully meets performance expectations, they will receive a confirmation letter from HR, officially acknowledging them as a permanent employee and recognizing their contributions to the team.
## Internal Communication for Employee Mobility
## Promoting career growth within the company:
- At Gloster Limited, we encourage internal mobility, meaning employees are always welcome to explore different roles within the organization. Job vacancies are communicated internally through email newsletters, the company intranet, and team meetings, giving all employees the opportunity to apply for new positions.
- Internal Candidates: Internal employees are given priority in applying for new roles, providing them with growth opportunities to advance or change career paths within the company. This encourages employee retention and promotes career development.
- Support during Internal Transfers: Employees who apply for internal job changes undergo the same interview process as external candidates, ensuring fairness and equal opportunity. HR and the hiring team provide guidance and ensure the process is smooth for all applicants.
## Policy on Original Documents
## Ensuring transparency and security:
- Gloster Limited ensures that we do not retain any original documents from candidates or employees during the recruitment process, providing transparency and ensuring that candidates feel their privacy is respected and upheld throughout their employment journey.
## Record Keeping and Compliance
## Managing records securely:
- All recruitment-related records are securely stored and maintained according to data protection laws and the company’s internal policies, ensuring confidentiality and compliance with privacy standards.
- Recruitment records are periodically reviewed and audited to ensure the process remains fair, transparent, and compliant with regulatory standards, ensuring that hiring practices uphold the highest levels of integrity and professionalism.

## Compensation and Annual Revision Policy
The compensation and benefits framework is vital for Gloster Limited, directly impacting our ability to attract and retain top talent in both the short and long term. As a growing company in India, achieving success requires us to maintain a competitive edge over our competitors, which means developing a strong position in the marketplace. Employees are essential to this competitive advantage, and effective talent management is crucial in ensuring we remain ahead in the global market. Since compensation plays a central role in attracting and retaining skilled professionals, managing it effectively is key to securing the best talent for our organization.
Gloster Limited ensures that all employees receive wages that meet or exceed the legally mandated minimum wage standards, as set by government regulations. Additionally, we are committed to ensuring gender pay equality, guaranteeing that employees are paid fairly and equitably, regardless of gender.
To maintain competitiveness, the company will review pay and benefits annually. This process will take into account various factors, including the business environment, financial situation, ability to pay, sales forecasts, market trends, competitor pay rates, individual performance, experience, length of service, and both internal and external equity. Our goal is to balance offering competitive pay for key positions with maintaining efficiency, sustainability, and competitiveness in overall manpower costs. Employee compensation will be determined based on the following criteria:
- Importance and criticality of the position
- Responsibilities and deliverables of the role
- Relevant prior experience
- Individual performance and competencies
- Qualifications and educational background
- Availability of talent in the market
- Compensation trends in the market and among competitors
- Internal pay equity
- Work location

At Gloster Limited, we are committed to ensuring that our compensation revisions are fair, transparent, and based on merit. The following parameters will not be considered when determining salary revisions:
- Gender
- Ethnicity
- Religion
- Domicile
- Caste
- Political affiliation
## Annual Compensation Revision
- Frequency of Revision: Salary revisions are conducted annually for all employees. The revision typically takes effect on April 1st of each year, based on performance during the preceding financial year (April-March).
- Eligibility: Employees who join on or before September 30th will be eligible for the revision in the ongoing financial year.
- Performance-Based Revision: The salary revision is directly linked to individual performance, as determined by the annual Performance Appraisal. The HR Department will review and moderate the performance ratings, and the final revision percentage will be endorsed by the HR Head or Chief Managing Director (CMD).
- Revision Determination: The percentage of revision will depend on:
- Individual Performance: As indicated by the annual performance rating.
- Business Performance: The overall performance of the organization.
- Annual Revision Grid: The HR Department will prepare a grid outlining the standard revision percentages for different performance levels, which will be endorsed by the HR Head or CMD.

chapters.title: Wage Equality
chapters.text:
- Gloster Limited is committed to providing equal pay for equal work, ensuring all employees are compensated fairly for the work they perform, regardless of gender, race, or other personal characteristics.
- A comprehensive wage gap report will be generated annually to provide transparency, highlight any disparities, and track progress toward achieving wage equality across all levels of the company.
- The company follows a structured approach to evaluate roles and responsibilities, ensuring that employees performing the same job or work of equal value receive equal pay. Disparities in pay will be addressed through regular salary audits and adjustments as necessary.
- All pay decisions, including promotions, raises, and bonuses, will be based on objective criteria such as skills, experience, performance, and job requirements, rather than personal characteristics or biases.
- The company will provide training to managers and employees on recognizing and eliminating unconscious bias in compensation decisions, reinforcing the principle of fair treatment in all wage-related matters.
- Gloster Limited will utilize the IDH Wage Analysis tool to assess and compare wage structures across various departments and roles, ensuring that pay equity is maintained across all levels of the organization.
- The IDH Wage Analysis will provide insights into potential wage gaps, helping to inform decisions on necessary adjustments to ensure fair and competitive compensation in alignment with industry standards.
- Gloster Limited is committed to regularly reviewing compensation practices to ensure that wage equality is consistently maintained and that any discrepancies are corrected.
- Employees are encouraged to bring forward any concerns about wage inequality to the HR Department, where they will be handled with confidentiality and prompt attention.
- Employees who believe they are being paid unfairly may request a formal review of their compensation by submitting a request to the HR Department for further investigation.
- Any identified wage disparities that are found to be discriminatory or unfair will be corrected, and necessary steps will be taken to ensure compliance with legal requirements and organizational standards on wage equality.
- Offer Letter Salary: The salary mentioned in your offer letter is the starting point for your compensation. This amount is clearly defined based on your position, qualifications, experience, and industry standards.
- Online Company Portal: Employees can view their current salary, benefits, and other compensation details through the company's secure online portal. This portal provides real-time access to your salary breakdown, including base pay, allowances, bonuses, and other compensations.
- Salary Bands: Salaries are organized into defined bands based on role and experience. These bands ensure that salaries are competitive and fair within the industry and are aligned with your job level. The band you fall within is outlined in your offer letter and can be referenced at any time via the online portal.
## Performance-Based Increments
- Annual Performance Reviews: Salary increments are linked to annual performance reviews, where your achievements, contributions, and growth are assessed. A percentage increase in salary is determined based on these evaluations.
- Review and Update Process: Performance reviews and salary adjustments are communicated transparently via the online portal and through one-on-one meetings with your manager. If you are eligible for a salary increase, it will be clearly stated in your review documents and updated on the portal.
## Bonuses and Incentives
- Annual Bonus: Employees may be eligible for an annual performance-based bonus, which is tied to company and individual performance metrics. Details of eligibility, criteria, and payout are outlined at the beginning of each fiscal year, and bonuses will be reflected on the employee’s payslip.
- Spot Awards and Special Incentives: Exceptional contributions may be rewarded through spot awards or other special incentives. Information about such incentives is communicated via internal announcements and can be accessed through the company portal.
- Overtime Compensation: If applicable, overtime hours worked will be compensated at the appropriate rate and reflected in the monthly payslip. The online portal will display overtime details for transparency.
## Leave and Time-Off
- Leave Balances: Your leave balance (annual leave, sick leave, etc.) is tracked and updated regularly in the online portal. You can view your leave status and apply for leave directly through the portal.
- Leave Approval: All leave requests must be submitted via the portal. Once approved by your supervisor, the leave will be reflected in your payroll calculations.

chapters.title: Overtime
chapters.text:
- Overtime work is any time worked beyond the standard working hours. Employees are required to record all overtime hours using the ARS system to ensure accurate tracking and compensation.
- Overtime is compensated at 1.5 times the standard hourly wage for hours worked beyond the regular daily schedule. Employees should seek prior authorization from their supervisor before working overtime.
- The ARS system will reflect overtime hours and wages in the employee's payroll, ensuring that compensation aligns with Gloster Limited's compensation policies and legal requirements.
- In case of any discrepancies or issues with overtime calculations or wages, employees must promptly report them to the HR Department for resolution.
- Any overtime worked beyond the regular schedule must be justified and approved by the respective department head. Employees should ensure they complete overtime hours only when necessary, and in alignment with operational needs.
- Employees will be required to submit a formal request and receive approval from their supervisor for any overtime that extends beyond the standard workday. Any unapproved overtime may be subject to non-compensation.
- Terms and Conditions:
- All overtime worked must be approved in advance by the Head of Department. This request shall be in writing. Only in exceptional circumstances (e.g., a meeting with a client that runs late, a pressing deadline, Audit etc.) can this request be made at the last minute. The Head of department will evaluate last minute requests on a case-by-case basis. An employee who works overtime without prior approval may be subject to corrective action.
- Whenever feasible, efforts should be made to avoid accruing compensatory time by adjusting the employees' work hours within the same work week.
- Shift Change for Personal work cannot relate to Overtime.
## Career Development and Promotion
At Gloster Limited, we believe in nurturing employees’ careers based on their performance, potential, and merit.
- Promotion Eligibility: Employees may be promoted to the next level based on an evaluation of their performance and work conduct throughout the year. This evaluation will consider the following criteria:
- Ratings and feedback from the immediate supervisor over the past year.
- Overall behavior and professionalism displayed in the workplace.
- Adherence to safety norms and standards throughout the year.
- Reviews and comments received from supervisors or Heads of Departments (HODs).
- Availability of higher-level roles within the organization.
- Merit-Based Promotion: Career growth and promotion will be based solely on merit, with unbiased assessments ensuring equal opportunity for all employees. No discrimination will be tolerated in the promotion process, and all decisions will be made with fairness and transparency.
- Promotion Timing: Promotion cases will be evaluated during the annual salary revision cycle. However, the final decision on promotions and salary revisions rests with the Senior Leadership Team and Management.
## Promoting Career Mobility
At Gloster Limited, we believe in empowering our employees through internal career mobility, offering them opportunities to grow and develop across different roles within the organization. Our approach is designed to support professional advancement, foster continuous learning, and align individual goals with the company’s objectives.
## Promotion to New Roles
- Employees who demonstrate the ability, potential, and outstanding performance to excel in new roles are given the support needed for a smooth transition. We offer relevant training and guidance, ensuring that employees are fully prepared to take on new challenges and responsibilities. Our promotion pathways are based on merit and are designed to help employees reach their full potential.
## nternal Opportunities for Career Advancement
- We actively promote career growth within the organization by encouraging employees to pursue various roles that align with their skills, aspirations, and professional goals. Employees are encouraged to apply for higher-level positions as they become available, providing a clear pathway for advancement. We prioritize internal job postings to ensure our employees have the opportunity to grow within the company.
## ertical, Horizontal, and Transversal Mobility
- Vertical Mobility: Through our structured promotion pathways, employees are given the opportunity to advance to higher-level roles. Performance reviews and development discussions help identify potential candidates for promotion.
- Horizontal Mobility: We support cross-departmental transfers, allowing employees to broaden their experience and diversify their skill set. This initiative encourages collaboration and innovation across different functions within the organization.

chapters.title: Paternity Leave:
chapters.text:
- Eligibility: Permanent male employees are entitled to two days of paternity leave, effective from the date of childbirth. This leave is applicable for a maximum of two children only.
## Additional Weekly Off:
- Eligibility: Deputy Managers and above will receive two additional weekly offs per month, as per government regulations.
## Leave Without Pay (LWP):
- Eligibility: LWP can be availed when other leave types are unavailable or exhausted. A maximum of 30 days of LWP can be taken with prior approval from the Department Head.
## Shift Change:
- Monthly Shift Schedule: The monthly shift schedule must be assigned via the online system within 4 working days of the start of each month.
- Emergency Shift Changes: Up to three emergency shift changes per month may be approved, provided they are not related to routine personal activities. Prior approval from the Department Head is required through the online system.
## Weekly Off Change:
- Emergency Off Change: One off change per month is allowed in cases of emergency, subject to prior approval from the Department Head through the online system.
- Weekly Off Assignment: Weekly off days will be assigned through the online system within 4 working days of the start of each month. A maximum of 4-5 weekly offs can be taken per month, depending on the length of the month.
- Intervening Weekly Off & LWP: Any weekly off or paid holiday falling within a period of absenteeism or LWP will be treated as an absence.

chapters.title: Bonus:
chapters.text:
- Eligibility: Employees who have worked a minimum of 30 working days during the year are eligible for a bonus. The bonus year is from 1st April to 31st March.
- Bonus Calculation: Employees with a basic salary of up to Rs. 10,000 are eligible for a minimum bonus of 8.33% of the higher of salary or basic wages earned during the accounting year.
- Payment of Bonus: Bonus will be paid within 8 months from the end of the accounting year. Employees who leave the organization during the year will receive their bonus as part of the full and final settlement.

## Attendance Recording and Working Hours Policy - Gloster Limited
- All employees must record their daily attendance to ensure accurate payroll processing. Employees are required to clock in and out at designated locations using the Attendance Recording System (ARS), which may include Face Recognition or Touch Screen Machines, available at the Company's Factory, Offices, and other locations. This policy aims to streamline the attendance recording process while fostering a culture of trust, integrity, and self-discipline.
- Employees are expected to clock in and clock out at their scheduled shift times using the ARS machines at the provided locations. In case of power failure or technical issues with the ARS machines, employees must manually sign the attendance register, indicating the time of arrival and departure.
- As part of maintaining discipline and punctuality, employees should ensure they are present at work well before their shifts begin. All Heads of Department (HOD) are required to maintain a minimum of 8 hours of presence throughout the day, at any time.
- To accommodate unavoidable situations (e.g., vehicle breakdown, traffic jams, personal matters), employees are allowed up to 15 minutes of lateness up to 3 times per month. Any further delays will be considered late and will result in a leave deduction (from CL, SL, or PL). If no leave balance is available, it will be treated as Leave Without Pay (LWP). Employees are expected to inform their managers or colleagues of delays promptly. Employees may also arrive late or leave early for up to 2 hours, but no more than twice per month (maximum of 2 hours per occasion). Any lateness beyond two occasions will lead to a salary deduction for the late hours or require the employee to apply for a half-day leave. This option is not a quota and should be used only in case of emergencies.
- A minimum of 3.5 hours of attendance is required on any given day to be counted as a half-day. If attendance is less than 3.5 hours, it will be considered a full day of absence, subject to the grace period rule. Any lateness or early departure of more than 2 hours will result in being marked absent for a half-day.
- If an employee leaves the office or factory for official or personal work during working hours, they must apply for a Gate Pass—Official Duty Gate Pass for official tasks and Personal Gate Pass for personal tasks. The employee must also swipe their attendance card or mark attendance through the ARS system when leaving and returning to the office or factory.
- If an employee is out for official work and is unable to return before office hours end, they are not required to return just to mark attendance. They can regularize their attendance the following working day by obtaining approval/remarks from their superior on the Gate Pass and updating their attendance online.
- For employees traveling for domestic, international, or off-site work, their attendance will be regularized by the HR Department based on the Travel Indent Form and approval from the respective HOD.
- Employees are expected to plan and apply for leave in advance to ensure attendance is regularized before they proceed on leave.
- In case of emergency or exigency where leave applications cannot be submitted before taking leave, the HR Department will accept the leave application up to a maximum of four working days after the employee returns to work. Any leave application submitted beyond this period will be marked as absent without pay.

chapters.title: Flexible work arrangements
chapters.text:
This section outlines the flexible working arrangements framework at Gloster Limited, aiming to promote a healthy work-life balance for employees while ensuring that operational needs and business goals are met. The responsibilities of employees and managers are defined to support the effective implementation of these arrangements.
This framework applies to all employees of Gloster Limited across all levels, including those directly or indirectly impacted by the company’s operations.
## Types of Flexible Arrangements
- Flexitime: Flexitime allows employees to adjust their start and end times within a set window. This option accommodates personal commitments such as childcare, eldercare, or long commutes. Departmental requirements and project deadlines will be taken into account before approval.
- Remote Work: Remote work permits employees to work from locations other than the office, such as their homes or co-working spaces. This arrangement is contingent on the availability of necessary equipment and technology to support remote work.
- Job Sharing: Job sharing allows two or more employees to share the responsibilities of a single full-time role. Each employee works part-time, ensuring coverage of the role while supporting reduced work hours, offering career growth opportunities for those wishing to reduce their hours.
## Eligibility
Employees must meet the following criteria to qualify for flexible working arrangements:
- Have completed at least six months of continuous service at Gloster Limited.
- Demonstrate the ability to meet performance expectations and maintain productivity.
- Have no ongoing disciplinary actions or performance improvement plans.
- Hold a role that is suitable for the requested flexible arrangement, as determined by the department head.
- Have access to the required resources and technology for the arrangement.
## Responsibilities
## Employees
- Maintain consistent productivity and time management.
- Communicate work schedules and any changes to their manager and colleagues.
- Adhere to in-office days and attend mandatory meetings as required.
- Demonstrate professionalism in all communication, including emails, phone calls, and video conferences.
- Follow data security protocols to safeguard sensitive company information.
- Report any issues or challenges with the flexible work arrangement promptly.
## Department Heads
- Set clear expectations, including core working hours and deliverables.
- Ensure that remote employees have the necessary tools and software for efficient work.
- Regularly review employee performance and provide constructive feedback.
- Encourage collaboration using communication tools, even for remote workers.
- Monitor the effectiveness of flexible work arrangements and adjust as necessary.
- Schedule regular check-ins to discuss progress and address any concerns.
- Ensure employees have access to ongoing training for skill development and career advancement.
- Facilitate communication between remote and office-based employees to ensure alignment.
## Application & Approval
- Request Submission: Employees wishing to request flexible work arrangements must submit a request via the designated online form or directly to their department head or HR. The request should include:
- The type of flexible arrangement (e.g., flexitime, remote work, or job sharing).
- The proposed schedule (e.g., start and end times for flexitime or days of the week for remote work).
- The justification for the request (e.g., childcare, health reasons, or long commute).
- A plan for maintaining productivity and communication.
## Approval Process:
- The department head will review the request within 2 business days.
- HR will make the final decision within 1-2 business days after reviewing the request.
- The employee will be notified of the decision within 3-4 business days, with an explanation of the reasons for approval or rejection.
- If approved, a trial period of 1-3 months will be implemented to evaluate the effectiveness of the arrangement. During this period, employee performance and productivity will be monitored.
- After the trial period, a final review will determine whether the flexible arrangement will be made permanent, with feedback sessions scheduled between the employee and department head to address any issues.
## Guidelines for Employees
- Employees working remotely should establish a dedicated workspace to enhance productivity and minimize distractions.
- Clearly communicate your work schedules and availability to ensure effective coordination with your team and manager.
- Maintain reasonable response times during work hours to support collaboration.
- Attend in-person meetings or events when required to contribute to essential discussions and team cohesion.
- Ensure that work meets quality standards and deadlines.
- Properly maintain company-issued equipment and report any issues to avoid disruptions.

chapters.title: Health and Wellness Benefits & Insurance Policy
chapters.text:
Gloster Limited offers a comprehensive health and wellness program designed to support the physical and mental well-being of its employees, with a strong emphasis on preventive care, emergency support, and overall work-life balance. The following outlines the key benefits provided and the associated insurance coverage details:
## Health and Wellness Benefits:
- Comprehensive Medical Insurance: Gloster provides medical insurance with coverage up to ₹5,00,000 annually for each employee, covering hospitalization, surgeries, and treatment for both employees and their dependents (spouse, children, and parents). Employees can enhance their coverage at discounted premiums through the company’s health coverage partner.
- Cashless Treatment Network: Employees can access cashless treatment at over 5,000 hospitals across the country, ensuring smooth and efficient access to care during emergencies.
- Mental Health Support: Gloster values mental well-being and offers confidential counseling services through certified professionals. Employees are eligible for free therapy sessions and access stress management workshops.
- Fitness and Wellness Programs: The company encourages physical fitness by offering free gym memberships or fitness app subscriptions, on-site or virtual yoga and meditation sessions, and wellness challenges with fitness rewards.
- Annual Health Check-Ups: Employees and their dependents are entitled to free annual health screenings, including blood tests, vision checks, cholesterol monitoring, and other preventive diagnostics.
- Dental and Vision Coverage: In addition to medical coverage, optional dental and vision plans are available, covering routine dental work, eye exams, and prescription lenses.
- Wellness Resources and Seminars: Employees have access to a wellness platform with curated articles, videos, and self-help tools on fitness, nutrition, and mental health. Monthly wellness seminars with healthcare experts are also hosted.
- Critical Illness and Accident Insurance: Employees are automatically enrolled in critical illness insurance, which provides lump-sum payouts for conditions such as cancer, heart disease, or stroke. Accidental insurance covers medical expenses and loss of income, offering up to ₹10,00,000 in the case of permanent disability or death.
- Work-Life Balance Initiatives: Gloster promotes work-life balance with flexible work schedules, remote working options, and employee assistance programs (EAP) to support both personal and professional well-being.
## Health and Accident Insurance Coverage:
Objective: To provide comprehensive health and accident insurance coverage for eligible employees, addressing medical expenses, hospitalization, and accidents occurring during work or while commuting.
Scope: This policy applies to all full-time employees working in the office premises of Gloster Limited, who are not covered under the Employees' State Insurance Act, 1948.
Responsibility: The Head of HR & Administration is responsible for implementing this policy in collaboration with the Finance department and CEO.
Eligibility:
- Employees, their spouses, and up to two dependent children under 25 years.
- Employees may cover either both parents or both in-laws (up to 90 years), but not a combination of both.
- Employees must have completed a minimum of 90 days of continuous service with the company to be eligible for coverage.
Coverage Details:
- ₹5 Lakhs total medical insurance.
- ₹10 Lakhs total accidental insurance.
Coverage Inclusions:
- Medical expenses for daycare treatments, hospitalization, and domiciliary care.
- Optional Add-On Covers:
- Pre-existing conditions.
- Maternity expenses.
- Critical illness.
- Outpatient treatments.
- Dental treatments.
- Organ transplant expenses.
- Ambulance and air ambulance services.
- Health check-ups.
- Modern treatments.
- Wage loss compensation during hospitalization.
## Accident Insurance Coverage:
- Coverage includes accidental death, permanent or partial disability resulting from workplace accidents or commuting, and related medical expenses.
## Waiting Period:
- Pre-existing conditions are covered after 1 year.
- Maternity benefits are subject to a 9-month waiting period.
## Exclusions:
- Cosmetic treatments and dental care (unless linked to hospitalization).
- Self-inflicted injuries and voluntary pregnancy termination under 12 weeks.
- Full policy details for further exclusions.
## Payment Basis:
- Claims can be processed via cashless or reimbursement methods, depending on the sum insured.
## Cost Sharing:
- Employees may share costs for expenses exceeding sub-limits or room rent limits.
## Renewal & Cancellation:
- The policy can be renewed annually or canceled by either party with prior notice. Fraud or non-disclosure of key facts can lead to termination.
## Claims Procedure:
- Cashless claims are available at designated hospitals.
- Reimbursement claims must be submitted within 30 days of treatment.

chapters.title: Anti-Discrimination Policy
chapters.text:
- Equal Opportunity Employment: Gloster Limited is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to ensuring that all employment decisions—such as hiring, promotions, compensation, and training—are based on merit, qualifications, and job performance without regard to race, color, national origin, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, disability, religion, or any other characteristic protected by law.
- Prohibited Conduct: Discrimination in any form is prohibited. We do not tolerate unfair treatment or biased decisions based on any protected characteristics. Discrimination may take many forms, such as biased hiring practices, unequal pay, exclusion from career development opportunities, or any behavior that adversely affects an employee’s performance or well-being.
- Reasonable Accommodation: We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations for employees with disabilities and those requiring accommodations due to religious beliefs or practices. Employees should contact the Human Resources department to discuss their accommodation needs and explore solutions that do not impose undue hardship on the business.
- Policy Enforcement: We take all allegations of discrimination seriously. Each claim will be investigated thoroughly, and any employee found to have engaged in discriminatory behavior will face disciplinary action. Consequences may include counseling, warnings, suspension, or termination, depending on the severity of the conduct.
## Examples of Discrimination:
- Unequal Pay: A qualified employee receiving less pay than their colleagues performing the same job based on gender or ethnicity.
- Unequal Opportunities: A qualified employee being overlooked for a promotion based on their age or disability, despite their strong qualifications and performance.

chapters.title: Anti-Harassment Policy
chapters.text:
- Definition of Harassment: Harassment refers to any behavior, whether physical, verbal, or non-verbal, that creates a hostile, intimidating, or offensive work environment. This includes actions that demean, belittle, or otherwise harm an individual based on their protected characteristics, making it difficult for them to perform their job effectively.
## Types of Harassment:
- Sexual Harassment: Unwelcome sexual advances, inappropriate comments, physical gestures, or requests for sexual favors. This type of harassment creates an uncomfortable and unsafe environment for the individual being targeted.
- Bullying: Repeated, unreasonable actions intended to undermine or intimidate an individual. This can include verbal abuse, spreading false rumors, or deliberately sabotaging someone's work or reputation.
- Retaliation: Any adverse action taken against an employee who has reported harassment or participated in an investigation. Retaliation may include unjustified disciplinary actions, exclusion from team activities, or denial of career advancement opportunities.
## Examples of Harassment:
- Sexual Harassment: Sending inappropriate or unsolicited messages to a colleague, creating a hostile work environment.
- Bullying: Making derogatory comments about a colleague’s race or gender, undermining their performance and confidence.
- Retaliation: Taking disciplinary actions or sidelining an employee who reported harassment, deterring others from coming forward.
- Support for Victims: We offer support to employees who have experienced harassment, including counseling services and the option to adjust work arrangements if necessary. Ensuring that victims feel protected and supported is a key part of our commitment to maintaining a respectful work environment.
- Training and Education: Regular training sessions are conducted for all employees, focusing on our anti-discrimination and anti-harassment policies. The training educates employees on how to recognize harassment, the importance of reporting concerns, and how to foster a positive and inclusive workplace.
## Responsibilities and Compliance
- Employee Responsibilities: Every employee is expected to treat their colleagues with respect and fairness. Employees should report any observed or experienced discrimination or harassment to ensure it is addressed promptly and appropriately.
- Manager Responsibilities: Managers and supervisors play a critical role in maintaining a respectful work environment. They are responsible for ensuring their teams are aware of our anti-discrimination and anti-harassment policies, addressing any complaints, and taking proactive steps to prevent incidents. Managers must create a culture where employees feel comfortable voicing concerns without fear of reprisal.
- Monitoring and Review: We continuously review and update our anti-discrimination and anti-harassment practices to reflect any legal changes and the feedback from employees. This ongoing review ensures that our measures remain effective and relevant.
- Consequences for Violations: Any violation of our anti-discrimination or anti-harassment policies will lead to disciplinary action. Consequences may include counseling, reprimands, suspension, or termination, depending on the severity and nature of the offense. We are committed to upholding these standards to protect our employees.
## Preventive Measures
- Clear Communication of Policy: At Gloster Limited, all employees are provided with a copy of the Harassment Prevention Policy during onboarding and through regular training sessions. This ensures that everyone is well-informed about unacceptable behaviors and understands the potential consequences of such actions.
- Regular Risk Assessments: We conduct regular assessments to identify and evaluate any potential harassment risks within the workplace. This proactive approach helps us address vulnerabilities before they become significant issues.
- Anonymous Reporting Channels: To promote a safe reporting environment, we offer confidential and anonymous reporting options. This encourages employees to report any incidents of harassment without fear of retaliation.
- Active Monitoring: Gloster Limited implements monitoring systems to observe workplace interactions and detect behaviors that may indicate harassment. We hold regular feedback sessions to evaluate our workplace culture and address any emerging concerns promptly.
- Support Systems: We have established various support resources, such as peer support groups and counseling services, to assist employees who may need help in dealing with harassment or other workplace issues.

Gloster Limited takes all allegations of discrimination and harassment seriously. To ensure the reporting process is accessible and straightforward, we provide multiple channels for employees to raise concerns:

chapters.title: Training & Development
chapters.text:
## Objective:
The aim of this training program is to ensure that employees at Gloster Limited receive appropriate training to enhance their performance, specifically in Good Manufacturing Practices (cGMP) and their respective roles. The program ensures proper documentation of all training sessions and provides a structured procedure for identifying, planning, executing, and tracking employee training in the manufacturing and support functions.
## Scope:
This training approach applies to both new and existing employees, including permanent and contract staff working in various functions such as manufacturing, quality control, warehousing, engineering, and quality assurance at Gloster Limited's facilities.
## Roles and Responsibilities:
## Training Coordinator:
- Oversees the training process for new hires and ensures that on-the-job training is completed before employees start their routine tasks.
- Manages and schedules periodic cGMP training for all employees.
- Develops training plans for cGMP and functional training across various departments.
- Identifies and qualifies trainers within the company, ensuring that the training pool is adequately staffed.
- Coordinates the creation of training materials and facilitates training sessions.
- Tracks employee training progress and escalates issues when necessary.
## Department Training Coordinators:
- Responsible for identifying specific training needs related to departmental Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs).
- Monitors the progress of employees' training, ensuring timely completion, and reports any delays to the Training Coordinator.
## nstructors/Subject Matter Experts (SMEs):
- Conduct training sessions and share their expertise on relevant topics.
- Serve as primary trainers and facilitate knowledge transfer.
## Human Resources:
- Coordinates the induction training programs for new employees, both onsite and offsite.
- Ensures that all new hires complete the necessary induction and onboarding processes.
## Employees:
- Are responsible for completing all assigned training within the specified timelines.
- Participate actively in training sessions and engage with learning materials.
## Training Procedures:
- Training: This process involves the acquisition of knowledge, skills, and competencies required to improve performance in specific job functions. It includes theoretical and practical learning aimed at enhancing employee capabilities.
- Training Needs Identification (TNI): This process helps to identify the training requirements for each role. Training needs are documented and assigned to employees based on their job functions and personal development goals, ensuring that they are equipped to perform their tasks efficiently.
- Training Management System: The system is designed to manage the administration, delivery, documentation, tracking, and reporting of training programs. This includes classroom training, online sessions, e-learning, and other training resources.
## Training for New Permanent Employees:
- Induction Training: All new employees will undergo an initial induction program when joining Gloster Limited. This training introduces employees to the organization, its policies, and its core functions, as well as health, safety, and environmental protocols. A site-specific induction manual may be prepared for each department to tailor the training content.
- cGMP Training: All employees in roles related to manufacturing, quality control, warehousing, engineering, and quality assurance will receive basic cGMP training. This will cover the essential regulations and expectations surrounding good manufacturing practices, ensuring employees understand the quality standards required in their work.
- Job-Specific Training: New hires will be trained on procedures that are specific to their roles. This training will include SOPs that pertain to their job responsibilities. On-the-job training will be documented and tracked to ensure all necessary training is completed before employees begin their regular tasks.
## Specific Programmes
## Family-Supportive Programs
- Gloster Limited implements family-focused policies designed to help employees balance work and family responsibilities effectively.
- Flexible working hours are available to assist employees in managing family commitments.
- Regular family-oriented events and activities are organized to strengthen community ties and support among employees.
- Comprehensive maternity and paternity leave policies are in place to ensure that new parents receive adequate time off.
- Childcare support programs may be offered to ease the financial strain of childcare for employees.
- Eligible employees can access telecommuting options, allowing them to work remotely and better manage family obligations.
- Employee Assistance Programs (EAPs) are available, offering counseling and support for employees and their families during difficult times.

chapters.title: Recruitment and Selection
chapters.text:
- Strict recruitment procedures are followed, including psychological testing and background checks to select candidates suited to security roles. Candidates with experience in conflict resolution or high emotional intelligence are given preference.
## Ongoing Assessments and Evaluations
- Security personnel undergo regular performance evaluations focusing on adherence to use of force policies. These assessments help identify areas for improvement or the need for additional training.
## Monitoring and Accountability
- Body Cameras and Surveillance: All security personnel are required to wear body cameras during their shifts to ensure compliance with the use of force policy. Surveillance footage is regularly reviewed to assess adherence to the guidelines.
- Incident Reporting and Review: A protocol is in place for the immediate reporting of any use of force incidents. A review board, including external members, assesses the appropriateness of force used in these situations.
## Response to Incidents of Excessive Force
## mmediate Action
- Security personnel involved in excessive force incidents are placed on immediate administrative leave pending a full investigation. Affected individuals, whether employees or others, are provided with medical and psychological support.
## nvestigation
- All use of force incidents are thoroughly and transparently investigated to determine whether the actions taken were justified and in compliance with the established guidelines.
- Findings from the investigations are used to improve future training, policy updates, and the overall effectiveness of the security measures in place.

chapters.title: Grievance Resolution Procedure
chapters.text:
## Purpose
- The purpose of establishing this grievance resolution procedure is to provide employees with a formal and structured process to raise concerns related to their job, manager, or the work environment. These concerns can range from perceived unfair treatment to issues related to safety or discrimination. By offering a clear and transparent grievance process, Gloster Limited ensures that employees have a safe space to voice their issues, and these concerns are properly addressed. This procedure aims to identify and resolve workplace issues, thereby fostering a positive and productive work environment.
## Key Benefits
- Fairness and Accessibility: Ensures all employees have equal access to report concerns.
- Transparency: Promotes openness in addressing and resolving grievances.
- Problem Identification: Helps uncover underlying issues that may not be immediately visible.
- Risk Mitigation & Compliance: Reduces potential legal or financial risks associated with unresolved grievances.
- Better Decision-Making: Informed decisions based on facts, improving company policies and practices.
- Improved Workplace: Contributes to a more harmonious and productive environment.
- Enhanced Employee Engagement: Promotes a culture of trust and respect, increasing employee satisfaction.
- Strengthened Organizational Culture: Reinforces company values of fairness, inclusivity, and respect.
- Legal Protection and Reduced Liability: Provides legal safeguards by addressing concerns systematically and reducing the risk of legal disputes.
This includes all employees, regardless of their position, as well as contractors, suppliers, and community members impacted by the company’s operations.
## Definitions
- Grievance: A grievance refers to any work-related issue raised by an employee, perceived as unfair treatment, violation of rights, or any other workplace concern that is detrimental to their well-being, such as unsafe working conditions, unequal pay, harassment, or discrimination.
- Grievance Mechanism: This is the formal, structured process that Gloster Limited has put in place to ensure that grievances are addressed in a timely, fair, and confidential manner. The grievance mechanism ensures that employees’ concerns are heard and acted upon appropriately.
## Types of Grievances:
Employee grievances may vary but generally fall into the following categories:
- Pay and Benefits: Issues related to salary discrepancies, bonuses, benefits, or payroll errors.
- Working Conditions: Concerns about unsafe, unhealthy, or unpleasant work environments, or unfair scheduling practices.
- Treatment: Issues such as harassment, discrimination, bullying, or lack of recognition from management.
- Workload: Feelings of being overwhelmed with work, insufficient resources, or inadequate support to meet job expectations.
- Communication: Concerns about unclear communication, lack of feedback, or the perception that management is not listening to employees.
Other specific grievances that may arise include:

## Technology and IT Support Issues
- Reporting Methods: Employees can report grievances through various methods:
- Human Resources Department: The HR team is responsible for managing grievances. Employees are encouraged to report their issues using one of the following methods:
- Direct Reporting to HR Manager: Employees can directly approach HR or contact the HR Manager by email at hr@gloster.com.
- Department Head: In cases where it is deemed appropriate, employees can report grievances to their immediate department head.
- Grievance Reporting Boxes: To provide anonymity, employees can submit written grievances using designated reporting boxes placed throughout the company premises.
- Record Keeping: For transparency and to ensure a fair resolution process, all grievances and their resolutions will be documented systematically. This includes:
- Filing System: Each grievance will have a separate folder that includes details like the employee’s name (unless reported anonymously), a brief description of the issue, and a chronological history of the grievance.
- Electronic Storage: All electronic records related to grievances will be stored securely, using encryption to ensure that only authorized personnel have access to the data.
- Backup: Regular backups of grievance records will be performed quarterly to ensure data security.
## Key Documents to Retain:
- The initial grievance form or complaint.
- Correspondence, meeting notes, and emails.
- Investigation materials such as witness statements and evidence.

chapters.title: Whistleblower Procedure
chapters.text:
## Purpose
The purpose of this Whistleblower Procedure is to establish a secure and efficient framework that enables employees and external parties to report ethical concerns in a timely manner. Gloster Limited is dedicated to fostering a culture of integrity, transparency, and accountability. This procedure aims to safeguard the company’s reputation, assets, and stakeholders’ interests while upholding the highest ethical standards in all operations.
## Scope
This procedure applies to all individuals associated with Gloster Limited, including employees (full-time, part-time, contract), consultants, vendors, suppliers, and any other third parties engaged in activities with Gloster Limited. It covers all company locations, ensuring uniformity and consistency in addressing ethical issues.
## Reporting Criteria
Concerns that should be reported under this procedure include, but are not limited to:
- Corruption: Any form of bribery, extortion, fraud, embezzlement, or other financial misconduct that undermines the integrity or financial stability of Gloster Limited.
- Bribery: Offering, accepting, or soliciting anything of value to influence business decisions improperly, including actions involving public officials, private sector representatives, or internal stakeholders.
- Information Security: Unauthorized access, data breaches, malicious software, or any violations of Gloster’s IT security policies that compromise data integrity or confidentiality.
- Discrimination and Harassment: Any violation of equal employment opportunity laws, harassment policies, or discriminatory practices based on race, gender, age, religion, disability, sexual orientation, or any other protected characteristic.
- Policy Violations: Breaches of internal procedures, ethical standards, or policies that could damage Gloster Limited’s reputation, present legal risks, or reduce operational effectiveness.
## Reporting Channels
Gloster Limited offers various reporting options to ensure accessibility and confidentiality:
- Direct Reporting: Employees and third parties may report concerns directly to senior management or the HR.
- Contact: +91 3322309601
- Anonymous Reporting: Concerns can be reported anonymously via email. Gloster ensures anonymity to the fullest extent permitted by law and practical considerations. Email: complain@glosterjute.com
## Procedure
- Initial Assessment: The HR team will evaluate the validity and seriousness of the reported concern within 2 business days to determine the appropriate action.
- Evidence Gathering: All relevant evidence, such as documents, electronic data, and witness statements, will be collected and preserved within 5 business days.
- Interviews: Interviews with witnesses or those involved will be conducted within 10 business days to gather additional details.
- Analysis and Review: The evidence and interview findings will be analyzed within 7 business days to assess their implications and potential outcomes.
- Actions and Resolution: Based on the investigation findings, HR will determine appropriate actions within 15 business days of starting the investigation.
- Reporting Outcomes: The findings of the investigation and any actions taken will be communicated to the individual who made the complaint within 3 business days of HR’s decision.
## Responsibilities
- Employees:
- Report any suspected ethical violations in good faith and provide detailed information and evidence where possible.
- Fully cooperate with the investigation and maintain confidentiality.
- Avoid making false or malicious accusations, as this may lead to disciplinary action.
- Management:
- Ensure all employees and third parties are aware of this procedure, including reporting channels and protections under the policy.
- Take all reports seriously, conducting thorough and impartial investigations in a timely manner.
- Ensure appropriate actions are taken based on investigation outcomes, including corrective actions or policy revisions.
## Confidentiality and Non-Retaliation
- Confidentiality: Gloster Limited is committed to maintaining the confidentiality of all parties involved in the reporting and investigation process, to the extent possible, consistent with the need for an effective investigation. Information will be disclosed only to those authorized and involved in the investigation.
- Non-Retaliation: Gloster prohibits retaliation against any individual who reports ethical concerns in good faith. Retaliation includes termination, demotion, harassment, or any adverse action against the whistleblower. Retaliation will be investigated and may result in disciplinary measures, including termination of employment or contracts.
